comment.narrative: Exchanges between HRDs from Aceh Timor Leste Mindanao have taken place over the last decade yet the Action intends to be more inclusive in the selection of participants women PwDs with a pronounced minority rights angle.
85 50 women in Y2 and Y3.

Y1 total achieved 0Y2 total achieved 85.7 42.9 womenA1.4 Out of 7 respondents 71.4 42.9 women of respondents reported that they benefited from the regional exchange and collaboration with peers from other organizations at significant level 14.3 reported they benefited at high level and 14.3 reported they benefited at moderate level.57.1 of them reported that their collaboration with peers have increased their understanding confidence and trust at significant level 28.6 reported an increase in high level and 14.3 reported an increase in moderate level. A participant said that lessons learned during the trip can be applied in their work. Some issues that CSOs in Indonesia have been working on are interesting and applicable in SBP. Other participants highlighted their key takeaway from Indonesian CSOs working together as a network can help to strengthen the work. Lastly participants with disabilities stated that they gained experience and guidance for building capacity of PwDs in SBP. Participants were selected through a process of nomination within our key network members primarily two project partners IPSKTA and year one subgrantees. Participants were selected to ensure fair representation among network members gender balance and PwD representation.

Y1 total achieved 3Y2 total achieved 31 oral statement was made at the United Nation Forum on Minority Issues UNFMI by Sukree Aitae a disability rights and Malay minority rights advocate from the Inclusive Learning Centre on Disabilities in Southern Border Provinces ILCD part of the Foundation for the Empowerment of People with Disabilities FEPD. His statement addressed issues affecting the marginalized disability community or minorities within minorities. He highlighted the total lack of employment opportunities for PwDs in the region amid a poor access to healthcare and education. He mentioned how Malay Muslims with disabilities are facing these issues alongside the structural neglect within welfare mechanisms and excluded from all policy decisions in the peace dialogue process. On October 11 2023 the House of Representatives voted to approve the establishment of the Adhoc Committee on Studying Monitoring and Promoting Peacebuilding in SBP. The adhoc committee consisted of 35 members including 8 government representatives and 27 politicians from 8 political parties. Many committee members and subcommittee members are from many CSOs working with the project. They were assigned to conduct a 90day study. The urgent motion was proposed by Romadon Panjor a MP from the main opposition Moving Forward Party alongside with other similar motions submitted by other MPs demanding the legislature to play more crucial role in the ongoing Peace Process and sustainable peacebuilding in SBP. A land rights issue in Tambon Sri Banpot Sri Sakhorn District Narathiwat Province was raised in by MP for Narathiwat in a parliamentary meeting on January 26 2024. The issue has been advocated by Rural Initiatives for Community and Ecology Association under A3.6 Peacebuilding Grants.

1.The new Malaysian government led by Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim continues to commit to facilitate peace talks and appointed Zulkifli Zainal Abidin as the new facilitator of peace talks. Anwar stressed the insurgency is an internal issue for Thailand but pledged to do whatever is required to facilitate a peaceful solution during an official visit to Bangkok in February 2023. 2.The new Thai government led by Prime Minister Srettha appointed Chatchai Bangchuad one of the deputy secretariesgeneral of the National Security Council NSC as the new chief of the Thai Peace Dialogue Panel. He was involved in the previous delegation and became the very first civilian to lead the peace dialogue panel. The appointment guarantees a continuation of the Peace Dialogue. Although it may not bring any significant changes within his term yet it prevents dissolution of the dialogue initiative and allows academic CSOs and local people to continuously and closely monitor the dialogue progress. 3.The House of Representatives voted for an approval to establish the AdHoc Committee on Studying Monitoring and Promoting Peacebuilding in SBP following a motion jointly submitted by the Move Forward Party Pheu Thai Party Prachachart Party and Bhumjaithai Party. The AdHoc Committee consists of two subcommittees one for studying and enhancing productivity of the peace negotiation process and the other for dealing with public participation in the peace process. Several committee members and subcommittee members come from CSOs working with MRG under the Peacebuilding Grants including IPS Prof. Haji Sulong Foundation Duayjai Group Nusantara Foundation and KTA so we can consider that the project has had a direct impact on the creation and workings of this Committee Also A3.1 CSO Peace Network Meetings became a significant platform where findings and recommendations from CSOs community leaders and grassroot communities were consolidated and contributed to the study of the AdHoc Committee.4.The Cabinet during its meeting on 16 January 2024 approved the lifting of the state of emergency in two districts in the deep South as violent from unrest has generally eased. Deputy Prime Minister Somsak Thepsutin who chairs the Committee on the Administration of Emergency Situations said that the Government would consider scrapping the emergency decree entirely in 2027 if the southern situation greatly improved. However efforts must also be made to ensure security. For instance more talks will be held with neighboring countries for cooperation on various issues.
